app.title: From Snow to Reservoir
app.summary: A person picks a site and narrows the time window in a sidebar that every page shares. An overview page shows the site's drainage basin on a map with its glaciers, rivers and derived reservoir outline. Beside the map are summary cards giving the latest reservoir, snow and ice areas, each with its range and mean over the window. A time series page charts the water area and the stacked snow and ice areas over time. A scene browser lets the person choose a sensor and step through the dates to see the classified image behind each reading, with the raw tables underneath.

task.text: Monitor how reservoir water, seasonal snow and glacier ice areas change over time in a drainage basin, and check each reading against the satellite scene it came from.

data.text: Two per-date tables of class areas extracted from classified satellite scenes: radar-derived water and reservoir area, and optical-derived snow, snow-on-glacier and bare ice areas, with coverage and cloud percentages. Alongside them are static vector layers (basin outline, glacier polygons, river network, reservoir footprint) and one pre-rendered classified image per scene date.
data.item: one satellite acquisition date for one basin, with its class areas and its classified scene image

stage.text: monitoring areas derived from processed satellite time series, after classification and quality filtering

mechanism.text: A site picker and a time-range slider in the sidebar set the data for all three pages. The overview pairs a layered basin map with summary cards, the time series page shows tabbed line and stacked-area charts, and the scene browser shows each date's classified image on a map using a sensor toggle and a date slider, with raw tables in an expander.

field.text: satellite remote sensing of snow, glacier and reservoir extent in catchment hydrology

workflow.name: watch measured quantities over time for a site and check them against the source images

steps.step: choose the site and the time window to look at
steps.here: an 'Area of interest' dropdown picks the basin, and a two-handle 'Time range' slider cuts both the radar and optical series to the chosen dates on every page

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: the overview map draws the basin outline, glacier polygons, rivers scaled by flow order, the dam and the reservoir footprint, and can switch to a dark, satellite or terrain base layer

steps.step: read each latest value against its range and mean
steps.here: three cards give the latest reservoir, total snow and bare ice areas with their dates, the min–max range and the mean over the window, under a count of valid radar and optical scenes

tabs switch between a water chart (reservoir area as the main line, basin-wide water as a faint reference) and a stacked-area chart of seasonal snow, snow on glacier and bare ice, where cloudy dates show as gaps; hovering reads every series for a date
a Dataset radio picks the water or snow-and-ice product, and a date slider loads that scene's classified image onto a map with a colour legend
a 'Show raw data' expander lists both per-date tables, newest first

distinctive: two sensors split the work: radar gives the water signal and optical gives snow and ice, so each page and the scene browser keep them on separate series
every statistic and map layer is limited to the drainage basin above a dam, and glaciers and rivers outside the basin are clipped away
dates with too little coverage or too much cloud are left as gaps in the charts, not interpolated, so a data gap does not look like a real change
snow area is corrected for coverage, scaling the observed snow share to the whole non-glacier basin so dates with different coverage can be compared
each chart date links to a pre-rendered classified scene, so a reading can be checked against the image it came from
